To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the sum data rate of a multi-cell VLC system is improved by using JT-CoMP transmission and by using a visible or blue light optical filter at the PD.

(i) the achievable data rate is higher in the inner parts when FR is applied; (ii) the achievable data rates are higher in the cell-edge areas when JT-CoMP transmission is applied; (iii) a blue light optical filter can increase the data rate in the cell-center area; (iv) the data rate can be increased by using a visible light optical filter in the cell-edge area.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the achievable sum data rate in a VLC system with multiple users when phosphor-convertible white LEDs are used to provide simultaneous illumination and communication.

the design of an efficient VLC transmission scheme for indoor applications, which can provide high data rate and high coverage simultaneously, and it is based on the use of white LEDs as both illumination and communication sources.
a practical VLC system with multiple users and multiple LED panels.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of a blue light filter is recommended for FR transmission, while the use of a visible light filter is recommended to achieve higher data rates in JT-CoMP.
the use of optical filtering in front of the photodetector is not recommended in the case of ACO-OFDM, and that the best achievable data rate can be achieved by applying the hybrid scheme.
the use of blue light filters is not a good option in VLC, as it results in a significant degradation of the achievable data rates, especially when JT-CoMP transmission is employed.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, in order to improve the performance of a VLC network, it is necessary to use the available resources efficiently, and to apply coordinated multi-point transmission techniques.

JT-CoMP provides a better performance for the VLC systems with phosphor-converted LEDs, especially in cell-edge areas, and that the use of a visible light filter improves significantly the performance of FR, while the performance of JT-CoMP remains almost unaffected.
JT-CoMP is more suitable for indoor VLC systems than FR, since it can achieve a higher average data rate with a more homogeneous coverage, while FR achieves a higher peak data rate.
The main takeaway from our work is that
JT-CoMP is the best option to achieve a high data rate in VLC systems with multiple users.
the achievable data rate in VLC systems with phosphor-converted LED lamps can be improved using JT-CoMP transmission schemes.
the use of a visible or blue filter in front of PDs is not a viable option for VLC systems with multiple transmission points.
